_comment: Marking vocabulary + equivalence rules for normalize.py.
This is a UK HMG Government Security Classifications scheme (current +
legacy GPMS), plus the descriptors, national caveats and common allied
control markings seen in mixed defence/government corpora. Adapt freely:
the canonical KEYS are your standard output set - rename, add or remove
them to match your environment.
HOW MATCHING WORKS
* Case-insensitive, and '-', '/' and ':' are flattened to spaces, so one
spelling covers 'OFFICIAL SENSITIVE' / 'OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE' /
'OFFICIAL: SENSITIVE'. You only list genuinely different spellings.
* Per-word aliases are matched greedily, longest phrase first, and
COMPOSE automatically - define building blocks and any combination
works ('SECRET // NOFORN', 'OS NC LS', ...).
* 'equivalents' (below) are whole-string rules checked FIRST; use them
for glued shorthand that can't be parsed token-by-token ('OS NCLS').
* Tokens that match nothing are preserved in the result's 'unknown'
list (never dropped) - a handy way to find formats you haven't mapped.
APPLYING CHANGES
Restart the service (the file is read at startup), or call
normalize.reload_markings() in a long-running process. Then run
backfill_norm.py once to re-project existing clips.
TO TEST A STRING
python normalize.py "OS NCLS"  "Privileged data: LS NC"  "FOUO"
Single-letter abbreviations are deliberately avoided (a stray 'S'/'C'
would match too eagerly). If this file is missing or invalid, normalize.py
falls back to its built-in defaults.
_comment_classifications: canonical level -> accepted spellings. ORDER MATTERS: when a marker
carries more than one level, the one listed FIRST wins. List MOST
SENSITIVE first. The key (left side) is the standard form stored in the
marking_class column and shown in the 'LEVEL // CAVEAT' display string.
Rows 3-4 + PROTECT are pre-2014 legacy GPMS markings, kept so older
documents still resolve; delete them if your corpus is all post-2014.
_comment_caveats: canonical caveat/descriptor -> accepted spellings. Caveats compose with
a level and with each other and are de-duplicated, order-preserving. The
first group are UK OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE descriptors; the second are national
/ handling caveats; the last are common allied (US/NATO) control markings
that turn up in mixed corpora - drop the ones you never see.
Note: free-form releasability lists ('REL TO USA, GBR, AUS') can't be
enumerated here; only fixed forms like FIVE EYES are mapped, the rest land
in 'unknown' (add an equivalents rule for any you want to pin down).
_comment_equivalents: Whole-marker rules, checked BEFORE the per-word vocabulary, so they always
win. 'match' (string or list) is compared case/separator-insensitively, so
list only genuinely different spellings. Use these for glued shorthand the
token matcher can't split ('OS NCLS' -> the abbreviations are fused).
You can also use a rule to REMAP a whole legacy marking to your standard
set, e.g. fold legacy RESTRICTED into OFFICIAL-SENSITIVE:
(left commented/out here - the example assumes you keep RESTRICTED as its
own level above; enable it only if your policy maps the legacy scheme).
